name: React RSC RCE
tile_line: Only Next 16 apps returning typed arrays from use cache.
tldr: A React Server Components bug lets an attacker call a Server Action with their own arguments. Lab exploit public, no attacks. In Next.js only with Cache Components and a use cache function returning several typed arrays; upgrade to Next.js 16.4.1+.
summary: The bug is in how React Server Components package several typed arrays (binary data) in one response; React says it only affects "extremely rare cases". The arguments only matter if a Server Action does something dangerous with them. The fix has been out since 14 Oct; the CVE ID came on 10 Nov.

affected.label: Next.js 16.0.0 – 16.4.0
affected.text: Or `react-server-dom-webpack`, `-parcel` or `-turbopack` 19.0.0–19.0.8, 19.1.0–19.1.9, 19.2.0–19.2.8 or 19.3.0 in another Server Components setup. Next.js 15.x isn't affected by this bug. Apps whose React code doesn't use a server aren't affected.
affected.cmd: npm ls next react-server-dom-webpack react-server-dom-parcel react-server-dom-turbopack

affected.label: Cache Components is on
affected.text: The App Router with Cache Components (`cacheComponents: true` in the Next.js config).

affected.label: A `use cache` function returns typed arrays
affected.text: One that returns several typed arrays. Hash Security adds that they must be larger than 4 KB, share one buffer, and come with a value the attacker influences.

affected.label: A Server Action does something dangerous
affected.text: Running commands needs a Server Action that does something risky with the arguments the attacker supplies, per Hash Security; their lab app wraps a shell command in one.

do.label: Upgrade
do.text: Next.js 16.4.1 or later (16.4.5 also fixes the [Next.js image bug](/nextjs-image-rce/)). Other setups: `react-server-dom-*` 19.0.9, 19.1.10, 19.2.9 or 19.3.1. Next.js says to upgrade even if your app has no such function.

do.label: No workaround
do.text: Next.js says there's no workaround for apps with an affected `use cache` function.

sources.title: React GHSA-xqc2: affected and fixed react-server-dom versions, 'extremely rare'
Next.js GHSA-673q: Next 16.0.0–16.4.0, Cache Components, no workaround
CVE record: CVE-2026-126187, CISA assessment exploitation none
Hash Security: how the bug works, what a lab exploit needs
Next.js: v15.5.28 release notes (no typed-array fix needed)
Cloudflare Zero Wire: no exploitation reported as of 11 Nov
